title: Ceylon
capsule: The Kingdom of Dambadeniya was established in the Kurunegala district of Sri Lanka's North Western Province by Vijayabahu III, who chose the hill fortress of Dambadeniya as capital after the devastating invasions of Kalinga Magha in the early thirteenth century had driven the Sinhalese court inland from the coastal plains. Its greatest ruler, Parakramabahu II (1234–1269), reunified the Buddhist Sangha, expelled a South Indian force that had captured the Sacred Tooth Relic, and composed the Sinhala literary masterpiece Kausilumina, making his reign a celebrated era of vernacular letters. Subsequent kings moved the capital to Yapahuwa and then Kurunegala for defensive reasons; Parakramabahu III recovered the Tooth Relic again from the Pandyas in the late thirteenth century. The capital shifted definitively to Gampola around 1345, at which point the Dambadeniya period transitions into the Gampola kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core zone around Dambadeniya fortress is archaeologically confirmed; the kingdom's administrative extent in the surrounding districts is inferred from chronicle sources and is imprecisely mapped.
